findings.text: File backed fault handling entry validates requested file offset against current size and either reports access beyond end as bus error or supplies a locked cache folio page with major or minor accounting and retry signalling when locks were dropped.

Synchronous mapped readahead selects among disabled forced huge sequential executable and read around behaviours according to area access hints and readahead budget, with miss history able to suppress further prefetch for poorly correlated access.

Miss history is increased on synchronous mapped faults and decreased on asynchronous hits for ordinary mappings, while sequential and executable mappings bypass both adjustments to keep the counter symmetric and avoid distortion from racing faults on locked folios.

Huge page aware mapped readahead is enabled only when transparent huge support is present plus the area requests huge pages plus the address space supports large folios, with order capped at two megabyte equivalent and window aligned down and sized to one or two folios.

Executable mapped readahead uses an architecture preferred order, clamps the window inside area file offset bounds to avoid section padding, and disables asynchronous lookahead because of expected random access.

File fault handling acquires shared invalidation protection when the folio is absent or observed not current, retains it across allocation and direct input, and releases it before all returns except where retry handling centralises cleanup.

Cached folios are accepted only when still attached to the same address space and containing the requested index and within current size rechecked under lock, with mismatches discarded and lookup repeated.

Fault resolution distinguishes bus error beyond size, out of memory on allocation failure, fallback or no page when another path installed a mapping, locked success with page supplied, and retry when address range protection was released for input.

Small table installation serialises on the upper level lock, retests emptiness after acquiring it, accounts a new table, orders preparatory stores before publication, then consumes the preallocated table and releases the lock.

Locked areas with previously valid entries revalidate emptiness first without blocking and then under the table lock when still empty, reporting no page when another thread installed a mapping, using a helper that returns a table pointer plus its lock address without acquiring.

Large file mapping installation attempts to publish a single upper level entry for a suitably aligned large folio and returns fallback when conditions are unsuitable, out of memory when auxiliary table allocation fails, and success after publication and cache maintenance.

Upper level file mapping is refused for hardware or area disabled transparent huge pages, unsuitable area alignment or length, non upper level folio order, poisoned subpages, or a concurrently populated entry observed under lock.
Upper level installation holds the upper level lock from emptiness verification through reverse map accounting and optional table deposit until entry publication and cache update complete.

Write faults make entries writable and dirty only where area writability permits, with copy on write private mappings restricted to single page anonymous accounting while shared mappings use file reverse map accounting and preserve dirty state on already writable entries.
File reverse map accounting rejects anonymous folios and applies memory locking only when the mapped extent covers the whole folio, preventing partially mapped reclaim hazards.

Upper level fault mapping first honours an already installed huge entry, then attempts large mapping for eligible folios, otherwise installs a preallocated small table when available and reports whether further small mapping work is needed.

Small mapping of a large folio expands to the full folio only when file size coverage or shared memory semantics plus complete containment inside the area plus confinement to one upper level table all hold, with address and table cursor rewound accordingly.

Fault around installation skips poisoned pages and already occupied entries including special markers, installing only empty runs and leaving markers for dedicated fault paths, which suppresses surrounding prefetch when markers intervene.

Cache scanning for mappable folios ignores transient index states and non folio values and unobtainable or locked or relocated or split entries, requiring current non readahead stable attachment and size bounded position before returning a locked referenced folio.
Mapped readahead state comprises page budget, miss history, window start, window size, asynchronous size, and folio order, with synchronous and asynchronous paths updating complementary subsets.

Fault handling uses a descriptor linking the area, file offset, access kind, fault address, cache page, table anchors and locks, preallocated table storage, allocation mask, and preserved original entry for userfault evaluation.

New locked folio accounting marks folios locked, updates zone and event counters, and batches references under a per processor local lock, flushing the batch when full or when caching is unavailable or disabled.

New folio list placement asserts absence from reclaim lists and chooses locked handling exclusively for purely locked non special areas, otherwise joining normal reclaim, with a no operation variant when locking support is absent.
Userfault write protection is inherited from the original entry only when the area enables that feature and the original entry was valid and carried the marker.

Prefaulted entries outside the fault address default to young with an architecture override point that currently requests young, and instruction cache maintenance precedes publication for all installed ranges.

File fault resolution plus upper level table installation plus small range installation plus upper level file installation plus file reverse map plus reclaim list insertion are exposed for use by broader memory management fault paths.
Fault status values encode major versus minor, locked success, retry, bus error, out of memory, fallback, and no page conditions used to coordinate upper layer fault handling.
Huge page geometry uses upper level mask order and page count constants to align fault addresses and to size accounting and cache maintenance for large file mappings.

Readahead and direct folio input may release address range protection to avoid blocking, in which case the caller receives a pinned file reference and must retry fault handling with refreshed area state and proper reference release.

Architectures needing auxiliary table storage require a preallocated table for upper level file mapping, with allocation failure reported as out of memory and consumed storage counted as an additional table.
